task: Earn a single-initiation E. coli monosome input for same-object full-product capture and catalytic exit.
decision: Use physically purified initiation complexes followed by an elongation-only mixture. This is established for full-protein synthesis. The exact reporter/3xFLAG/spacer/UAG capture-release cycle remains a testable transfer, not a demonstrated complete operation.

sources.title: Polysomes Bypass a 50-Nucleotide Coding Gap Less Efficiently Than Monosomes Due to Attenuation of a 5′ mRNA Stem–Loop and Enhanced Drop-off
sources.location: In vitro monosome and polysome formation; Figure 4
observed: E. coli 70S initiation complexes were formed before elongation, then purified through a 1.1 M sucrose cushion.
Monosome reaction received purified initiation complexes and aa-tRNA/EF-Tu/EF-G/energy components. The polysome comparison explicitly added free 30S and 50S, initiation factors and initiator tRNA.
A full 160-aa bypass product was made in the monosome reaction. Specialized bypass efficiency is not a generic translation or recovery yield.

sources.title: Synonymous Codons Direct Cotranslational Folding toward Different Protein Conformations
sources.access: Full article and supplemental methods inspected from author institutional repository
observed: Full gamma-B crystallin synthesized in a fully reconstituted single-turnover E. coli translation system.

sources.scope_limit: The internal UAG used for FRET is deliberately decoded by amber suppressor tRNA. It is not evidence of a final-UAG stall or RF1-triggered release.

sources.title: Timing of GTP binding and hydrolysis by translation termination factor RF3

sources.title: Gradual compaction of the nascent peptide during cotranslational folding on the ribosome
observed: Stopless HemK nascent chains were retained in P-site peptidyl-tRNA complexes.
RNCs were purified from translation factors and free fluorescent tRNA through 2.2 M sucrose, 68,000 rpm, 40 min, 4°C; downstream fluorescence measurements used these RNCs.

sources.title: Single-molecule imaging of full protein synthesis by immobilized ribosomes
observed: Full GFP synthesized by immobilized E. coli ribosomes in ribosome-free PURE solution.
C-terminal spacer and SecM arrest sequence retained fluorescent protein co-localized with ribosomes; complexes were stable for hours.
sources.scope_limit: SecM arrest changes exit-tunnel/PTC state. Its lifetime is not a bound for a non-SecM UAG complex; SecM is not silently interchangeable with the RF1 gate.

sources.title: Full-protein release assay in a reconstituted yeast translation system using GGQ-methylated eRF1
observed: Full-length nanoluciferase peptidyl-tRNA complexes generated in yeast PURE by omitting release factors.
Release-factor addition generates active released nLuc; a functional full-protein release assay is prior art.
Uses CrPV IGR IRES initiation and yeast ribosomes/factors.

sources.title: A systematically-revised ribosome profiling method for bacteria reveals pauses at single-codon resolution
observed: Even 10,000 units RNase I did not collapse E. coli polysomes to monosomes in the authors' experiment.
E. coli ribosomes inhibit RNase I. MNase works for profiling but has sequence specificity.
RelE cleaves at the A-site codon.
sources.scope_limit: Footprints/sedimentation do not establish RF1 termination or reusable 50S function. RelE damages the stop-codon witness.

proposed_composition_not_a_published_end: Form initiation complexes on one-RBS reporter messages before elongation. Supply candidate 50S only in this phase with needed 30S; independently bound native-50S contamination.
Clear soluble initiation components using earned separation operations. Measure initiation occupancy. A cushion cannot distinguish empty 70S from occupied 70S.
Elongate with aa-tRNA, EF-Tu, EF-G and energy, with no newly supplied subunits, IFs, initiator tRNA, RF1/RF2 or rescue factors. Verify residual reinitiation rather than assuming perfect removal.
Adapt reporter/3xFLAG/spacer/UAG. Determine full peptidyl-tRNA abundance, UAG occupancy, no-RF retention and RF1-specific release. Stopless or SecM results cannot replace these tests.
If residual polysomes are material, collect and verify a monosome fraction before product capture. This adds separation, time and recovery costs whose values remain unknown.

2 h IC ultracentrifugation in the distinct ic_purification2014 source
40 min RNC pelleting in the distinct rnc_purification2020 source

source_derived.calculation: 50 µM / 0.016 µM; reagent provision, not consumption or a manufacturing optimum

costs_and_losses.prohibited_inference: Do not multiply borrowed source yields as if they belong to one compatible protocol.

reasons: RNase I failure is demonstrated; universal ribosome damage is not the justified general claim.
MNase may sever shared messages but has nonuniform digestion and no earned RF1/reuse endpoint here.
A nuclease route must preserve the stop codon and local decoding context, remove or quench nuclease, and demonstrate peptide-release plus subsequent translation.
RelE directly compromises the A-site codon and is unsuitable.

discriminating_measurements: Before elongation: initiation occupancy and free-initiator/IF carryover.
After elongation: reporter length, peptidyl-tRNA identity, stop occupancy, monosome/disome/polysome fractions and retained lifetime.
False-positive challenge: mix distinguishable active and inactive ribosomes before cohort formation and quantify inactive co-elution.
After capture: RF1 versus no-RF and RF2 at UAG; intact candidate 50S recovery.
After recovery: independent second message/stop context, with recovered mass and functional output reported jointly.
